subject: Interpretation of goodness of fit test

messages.author: 854cda7ec1519e04
messages.subject: Interpretation of goodness of fit test
parts:
Hello secr users,

I would like to check overdispersion of my dataset vs my top-ranked model. I have looked up several times the secr manual and the different threads of this group related to the topic, but I am still unsure about it, so I am turning to you for guidance.

From what I understood, I would need to run a goodness of fit test on my top-ranked model using secr.test and the statfn function given in the example, i.e:
bothfn <- function(object) 
                { CH <- object$capthist
                f1 <- sum(apply(abs(CH) > 0, 1, sum) == 1) / nrow(CH) 
                devdf <- deviance(object) / df.residual(object) c(f1 = f1, devdf = devdf)
                }
test <- secr.test (secrdemo.0, nsim = 19, statfn = bothfn, fit = TRUE) test plot(test, main = '') 
With secrdemo.0, I get the following results:
                    P
f1            0.65
devdf      0.60

Which means that the rank of the observed value in the vector combining the observed value and simulated values is 12. This is where I get stuck. How do you link these probabilities to goodness of fit and overdispersion? The greater P(devdf ), the better the fit?

Apologies if my question seems obvious.

Best wishes

Marie

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Interpretation of goodness of fit test
parts:
I think you can interpret P as the probability of observing a value that large under the null hypothesis that the data were generated under the fitted model. So small P (<0.05?) implies significant lack of fit. There is no canned measure of overdispersion. Goodness-of-fit and overdispersion have yet to be fully investigated for SECR models: I'm not claiming expertise here, just providing a tool.
Murray
